hook.line: You've asked twice and nothing happens. Spanish has a sharp third try: the order again, with *que* in front.
hook.en: I said be quiet, once and for all!

examples.en: I said be quiet, once and for all! (to a friend)
I said don't touch it! (to a friend)
I said come here! (to a friend)
I said come down now! (to a friend)
I said leave me alone! (to a friend)
I said turn the music off! (to a friend)

rule:
First time, you give a normal order: *Baja.* If it's ignored, you say it again with *que* and the changed ending: *¡Que bajes!* It means "I said...".

The frame is *¡Que* + changed ending + *!*. For no: *¡Que no lo toques!* Add *ya* or *de una vez* to sound angrier.

It's sharp. Use it with a sibling or a kid, not with your boss.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a repeated command: *que* plus the subjunctive for an order already given.

options: I said be quiet, once and for all!
Be quiet, once and for all!
I said I'll turn the music off!
I said turn the music off!

yourTurn.prompt: You've asked twice. Choose *Ven* or *Que vengas*, then type: ¡___ aquí ahora mismo! (I said come here right now! To a friend.)
Type it in Spanish: I said be quiet, once and for all! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te calles* is the changed ending, and *de una vez* adds the anger.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I said don't touch it! (to a friend)
Type it in Spanish: I said turn the music off! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Apagues* is the *you* form of the changed ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I said leave me alone! (to a friend)
Say it again, harder: *¡Baja ya!* becomes: I said come down now! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Same order, but now with *que* and the changed ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *¡Que te vayas!* becomes: I said don't go! (to a friend)

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que*, drop the command form and use the changed ending: *te calles*.
Almost. *Vienes* is a plain fact; *vengas* is the order.
Almost. *Que* is for the second try. The first time, give a plain polite order.

personal: Think of something you'd say twice to a kid, a sibling or a pet. Say it the third time with *¡Que...!*.
